definitions.gloss: loanword, borrowed word, word of foreign origin
definitions.explanation: A word adopted from a foreign language into Japanese. In practice, this term usually refers to words borrowed from Western languages (especially English), which are written in katakana. Words borrowed from Chinese ({漢語|かんご}) are generally not called {外来語|がいらいご}.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{外来語|がいらいご}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many loanwords in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 「コンピュータ」は{英語|えいご}からの{外来語|がいらいご}だ。
{最近|さいきん}は{外来語|がいらいご}が{増|ふ}えすぎて、{年配|ねんぱい}の{人|ひと}には{分|わ}かりにくいという{声|こえ}もある。
examples.english: Some say that loanwords have increased so much recently that they are hard for older people to understand.

notes:
USAGE:
Japanese vocabulary is classified into three categories: {和語|わご} (native Japanese words), {漢語|かんご} (Sino-Japanese words from Chinese), and {外来語|がいらいご} (loanwords from other languages). Despite Chinese being technically "foreign," {外来語|がいらいご} conventionally excludes {漢語|かんご} and refers mainly to Western borrowings written in katakana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外来語|がいらいご}を{使|つか}う: use a loanword
- {英語|えいご}からの{外来語|がいらいご}: loanword from English
- {外来語|がいらいご}{辞典|じてん}: loanword dictionary
- {外来語|がいらいご}の{乱用|らんよう}: overuse of loanwords

SIMILAR WORDS:
{外来語|がいらいご} is the standard linguistic term. カタカナ{語|ご} (katakana word) is a casual synonym. {借用語|しゃくようご} (borrowed word) is the more technical linguistic term.
